newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, CPO down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, CPO down.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were generally stable in late trading on Monday, but crude palm oil was sharply lower at a tender, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,460-65 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but offers were also heard at 1,450-55 rupiah. They said crude palm oil was done at an equivalent of 1,276 rupiah/kg at a 1,000-tonne tender at the North Sumatran city of Medan, against 1,303 rupiah previously.
The traders also said the market was digesting news that Malaysia was unlikely to maintain its palm oil production growth in 1997 due to labour shortages and lower yields.

Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) said in a report released in Dhaka on Monday as part of the Malaysia-sponsored Palm Oil Week only 7.6 million tonnes would be available for export this year, after meeting domestic consumption of 1.3 million tonnes and allowing for inventory.
Exports totalled 7.197 million tonnes in 1996. Output was expected to grow by 6.1 percent to 8.9 million tonnes in 1997 from 1996, when it grew by 7.4 percent over 1995, it said.
Indonesian traders said rumours that the Pakistani government was planning to reduce the import duty on edible oils by 1,000 rupees ($24.86) per tonne had no impact.
"Until it is confirmed, it will not have any impact on the market," one trader said. "Furthermore, Pakistan mostly does business with Malaysia."
Traders also said palm olein supply was tight in Jakarta, due, in part, to a surge in crude palm oil exports last month.
"I heard that February exports were very good, and it is likely to squeeze local supply and lift prices," one said.
